name: Proto-South Sulawesi
region: South Sulawesi; homeland placed on the lower Sa'dan river (p. 217)
orthography_note: Mills writes ë for the schwa (ə here), ng for ŋ and q for the glottal stop (ʔ here); his e is 'a low or mid front vowel' (n. 4, p. 208), not the PMP schwa. *R is 'presumably a voiced velar fricative' (p. 213); *z perhaps an affricate [dz], 'the voiced counterpart of *s' (p. 212).
notes: Mills (1975: 205): the ancestor of Buginese, Makassarese, Mandar, Sa'dan Toraja, Pitu Ulunna Salo, Seko and Massenrempulu', 'a minimum'. Nasal clusters *mp mb nt nd ñc ñj ŋk ŋg ns nz are reconstructed intervocalically only (p. 206); consonants after *ə were geminate (*tëllu 'three'), which Mills connects with a fixed penultimate stress (pp. 208-209); *q and *h are tentative, *q only in reduplicated monosyllabic roots (*buqbuk, *miqmis) and *h in two etyma (*(dr)ehde, *bahba) (§6, pp. 214-215). Final consonants *p t k m n ŋ r l s R (§5, p. 212); *-p is tentative (p. 213). '*(dr)' marks etyma with PAN *d or *D that show r in every daughter, where PSS *d or *r cannot be decided (pp. 210-211); '(C)' an unspecified final. The palatals may be loans in the three languages that keep them, so that 'PSS in fact had lost them' (p. 210). Mills states his PAN in Dempwolff's notation (*h for Dyen's *q, ë for the schwa); the PAN > PSS rows are restated against PMP (decision mills1975-pss). Mills's subgrouping (§8, pp. 217-218): Makassarese broke off first, before the change of nasal + voiceless stop to geminates, then Mandar, then Buginese; then 'Toraja, in the broadest sense, including PUS-Seko and Sa'dan', while Massenrempulu' stayed in the homeland, close to Sa'dan (71%). The daughters are entered directly under PSS (decision grimes1987-tree). Glottolog 5.4's South Sulawesi (sout3413) has no Seko and adds Tamanic; the Glottocode is left blank (decision mills1975-pss).

name: Bugis
region: South Sulawesi: the east coast, the central lakes and the west coast north of Maros
notes: Mills's Bug., from his field work and Matthes (1874). Mills reconstructs the b/w and d/r alternation after the prefix maq- (maqbere 'give' < were) as historical *b, *d > w, r in absolute initial position, retained after q (p. 211); there are many doublets, and the synchronic rule now also affects r from PAN *r, *R. Bug. -q alternates with r, s, k before the suffixes -ëng and -i (p. 212). Final consonants only q and ng (p. 212). Grimes & Grimes (1987: 15, 30-32): with Campalagian the Bugis Family; dialects Luwu, Wajo, Bone (Palakka), Soppeng, Enna' (Sinjai, Bulukumba), Sidrap, Barru, Sawitto, Pangkep, Camba, Pasangkayu.

name: Makasar
region: South Sulawesi: the south-west of the peninsula
notes: Mills's Mak., from Matthes (1859) and the Lembaga Bahasa Nasional. The final continuants r, l, s survive with an echo vowel and q (ukiriq < *ukir), so that synchronically Makasar has only final q and ng (pp. 212-213 and n. 11); -q > k before -ang and -i (p. 212). Mills calls Konjo and Salayar dialects of Makasar (p. 211); Grimes & Grimes (1987: 15, 25-29) make Makassar (dialects Maros-Pangkep, Gowa (Lakiung), Turatea (Jeneponto), Bantaeng), Konjo and Selayar a 'language chain', the Makassar Subfamily, and Jukes (2020: 20-21) separate languages. The sourced inventory is Jukes's (2020) Gowa (Lakiung) dialect.

name: Mandar
region: West Sulawesi: the coast from Polewali to Cenrana
notes: Mills's Mdr. is the Balanipa dialect of his field work, with the Campalagiang and Cendana dialects of Adriani & Kruijt (1914) and the Majene of Pelenkahu (1967) (p. 212, n. 10, 12). Final consonants q n ng r l s, the status of l doubtful and n merging with ng in Balanipa; Majene has q ng r l s (p. 212). -q is lost before -an/-ang (p. 213). Grimes & Grimes (1987: 15, 33-36): a dialect chain (Majene, Balanipa, Pamboang, Sendana, Awo' Sumakuyu, Malunda) in their Northern South Sulawesi Family; their Balanipa, Pamboang and Malunda have a voiced alveolar fricative with ungrooved blade for d (p. 96).

name: Toraja-Sa'dan
region: South Sulawesi: the upper Sa'dan valley
notes: Mills's Sad., from van der Veen's (1940) Tae' dictionary and van der Veen (1929). The outlying dialects (Mamasa, Mangki, Rongkong) differ from Makale-Rantepao 'mainly in the retention of palatals and intervocalic /w/' (p. 218). Final consonants q k n ng; -q alternates with r, s before -an (p. 212). Grimes & Grimes (1987: 15, 43-48): Toraja-Sa'dan (Makale, Rantepao, West Toraja) in their Toraja-Sa'dan Subfamily with Kalumpang, Mamasa, Rongkong and Toala'; Mamasa and Rongkong have an unreleased final [k̚] (p. 96).

name: Duri
notes: Mills's Mass. (Massenrempulu'), whose forms come mostly from the Duri dialects Cakke (DuriC) and Kalosi (DuriK) (p. 205 n. 1) and from Pelenkahu et al. (1972); entered on Duri, with the dialects as varieties (decision mills1975-lects). Final consonants q k n ng, Duri adding h (p. 212); a final -t reappears before -an (sirakatan, p. 214); *R and *-s have merged as h (p. 213). The Massenrempulu' lects measure over 80% with each other and 71% with Sa'dan (p. 218). Grimes & Grimes (1987: 15, 49-51): Duri (Cakke, Kalosi) is a dialect of Masenrempulu (with Maiwa and Enrekang) in their Masenrempulu Subfamily; Enrekang has a back velar nasal where other languages have a final k or glottal stop (p. 96).

name: Pitu Ulunna Salu
region: West Sulawesi: the upper Mamasa and Mambi rivers
notes: Mills's PUS, from his field work and van der Veen (1929) (PUS(V)); Glottolog's Pitu Ulunna Salu is a family (Aralle-Tabulahan, Bambam, Ulumanda' and others), entered here as one lect as Mills treats it (decision mills1975-lects). Final consonants q k n ng, some dialects m (p. 212). Grimes & Grimes (1987: 15, 39-42, 96): dialects Aralle-Tabulahan, Mambi, Rantebulahan, Bambang, Mehala'an, Tapango, Ulunda, in their Northern South Sulawesi Family; Aralle-Tabulahan, Mambi and Rantebulahan have [h] where Bambang and Mehala'an have [w]; Aralle-Tabulahan and Bambang have [h] for /r/; Bambang has [m] for every final nasal, the others [m], [n] or [ŋ]; Aralle-Tabulahan contrasts a low front lax vowel with [a].

name: Seko
region: South Sulawesi: the upper Karama river
notes: Mills's Seko, from word lists filled in by informants in the Lemo (SekoL) and Padang (SekoP) dialects; forms are 'sic' unless heard (p. 220). Geminates after *ə are simplified (p. 209). Final consonants q k ng, no n (p. 212). Glottolog 5.4's Seko is a family (Seko Padang seko1243, Seko Tengah seko1242, Panasuan) under Rampi-Seko-Badaic, outside its South Sulawesi; entered as one lect under PSS, the dialects as varieties (decision mills1975-lects). Grimes & Grimes (1987: 15, 52-53) have a Seko Family (Seko Tengah, Seko Padang, Panasuan) in their South Sulawesi Stock; Seko Tengah has long and short vowels word-finally (p. 97).
